newsitem.title: UK: Japanese stocks in London weaker on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Japanese stocks in London weaker on profit-taking.

text.p: The jump in Japanese shares in Tokyo overnight has encouraged some mild profit-taking in Europe on Monday as investors remained cautious about the Tokyo market's near-term prospects.
"We haven't seen a great deal of volume but the trend has been downwards," a dealer at a major Japanese investment bank said.
"People are using the opportunity of today's bounce in Japan to sell again."
In Tokyo on Monday, the Nikkei-225 gained 4.7 percent or 815.14 points to finish at 18,118.79.
Banking stocks in particular were under pressure after strong gains in Tokyo.

Sanwa Bank, which closed up 180 yen at 1,560 yen in Tokyo, was trading at 1,555 yen by 1320 GMT. Tokai Bank was at 995 yen after finishing up 93 yen at 1,000 in Tokyo, while Daiwa Bank eased to 550 yen from 551 yen.
Fuji Bank, the fourth most active share in Tokyo, up 140 yen to close at 1,550 yen was standing at 1,547.5 yen in London.
